Electric motors are devices that convert electrical energy into mechanical energy...
DISCUSSION
One type of electric motor is called the DC motor.
The DC motor uses Direct Current (DC) as its electrical power supply...
Let's see the basic principles of DC motor action..
First, a magnetic field is produced using two magnets......
Note that the magnets are stationary and not allowed to move toward each other...
A rotating magnet is placed between the other two magnets..
Because like poles repel and unlike poles attract, the center magnet rotates...
The attraction of unlike poles causes the center magnet to be drawn to the stationary magnets.
When the poles of the center magnet change, the like poles will repel and rotation will occur.
By continually changing the poles of the center magnet, motor action occurs...
What do like magnetic poles of two magnets do to each other?
Unlike poles attract toward each other.....................

The magnetic poles of two magnets will affect each other by either attraction (unlike poles) or repulsion (like poles).
This is basic motor action. However, the center magnet cannot be a permanent magnet.
Since the poles of a permanent magnet cannot be changed, an electromagnet is used.
By reversing the DC current flow, the poles of the center magnet change...
The center electromagnet is called the armature or rotor...
Why is an electromagnet used for motors?
The poles of a permanent magnet can be changed.
The poles of an electromagnet cannot be changed.
The poles of an electromagnet can be changed.
The poles of a permanent magnet are set, while electromagnetic poles can be changed.

The actual construction of the DC motor shows the armature as a coil, also known as windings.
A commutator rotates with the armature and is a copper or copper alloy cylinder split into segments with each segment insulated from one another and the shaft.
Each commutator segment is connected to an end of an armature winding...
Brushes make contact with the commutator and are normally made of a carbon compound to reduce friction.
The brushes are used to conduct current from the power source to the armature windings.
When a power source is connected to the armature, through the brushes and commutator, a magnetic field is produced.
This allows the direction of current flow to change each 1800 of rotation, reversing the poles in the armature.
Because the poles in the armature reverse, motor action occurs.
Since DC is applied, the rotating machine is a DC motor....
The schematic symbol for this type of DC motor shows the armature and brushes...
It is called a permanent magnet DC Motor because the armature is placed between two permanent magnets.
The stationary magnets are called the Stator.
The most commonly used type of DC Motor is the electromagnetic design...
Instead of a permanent magnet stator, an electromagnet stator is used...
The coils around the stator are the field windings.........
The field windings connect to the same power source as the armature (rotor) windings.
The way the field windings are connected produces the three types of Electromagnetic DC motors.
The field coil windings of a DC motor are represented as an inductor...
The schematic symbol for a basic Electromagnetic DC Series motor shows the brushes, armature, and includes the field coil.
The DC Shunt Field motor shows the field coil in parallel with the armature...
The DC Series Field motor shows the field coil in series with the armature...
The Compound motor contains a shunt and series field coil..

Using a series motor rotating in a clockwise direction, let's find out the two ways of changing rotational direction.
Reversing the direction of current in the armature is one way.
The other way is to reverse the direction of current in the series field...

One thing to remember is that reversing both the armature and the series field will not change the direction of the motor. Only the armature OR the series field can be reversed in order to change the rotation of the motor.....
Industrial applications sometimes require the ability of the motor to change directions.

A motor that is oversized (too large) will consume more current (power), increase the cost of the motor and amplifier, stress associated machinery, and lose some control which will cause the load to be moved too easily...

Now let's investigate motor start currents.................
When a motor is first turned on, there is 0 RPM and 0 CEMF.
Since CEMF is 0, the entire applied voltage is felt across the armature coils. Armature current is maximum.
As the motor begins to spin, armature current as well as total current drawn from the power source, will decrease due to the increasing CEMF.
In fact, some large motors have two sets of coils and wires that are controlled by a centrifugal switch.
A heavy-duty set of coils is used for starting the motor. This rates the motor for higher starting current.
A normal set of coils is used when the motor is running. This rates the motor for lower running current.
